subject: Pre-sales: session morphology, prompt/response lengths & quantization constraints
messages:
From: Simran Kaur <simran@orbitai.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Adam Li <adam@orbitai.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing help — session shapes + quantization limits

Hey Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. We're kicking off an evaluation for a customer-facing assistant that will run on dedicated capacity — primarily multi-turn chat, some batch generation for summaries. Topline asks:

- We need a quick estimate for committed GPU capacity (monthly) and guidance on quantization tradeoffs (int8 vs int4) for cost targets.
- Typical prompt lengths: 50-220 tokens. Typical responses: 30-400 tokens (median ~120).
- Peak concurrency is sketchy: looks like 650 concurrent sessions during US business hours with sharp 10-min spikes to ~1.8k.

I attached a small sample token distribution and a CSV with session timestamps. Happy to share more telemetry.

Can you run this through a sizing template and call out the biggest unknowns we should instrument?

Best,
Simran
Product Ops — OrbitAI
attachments: orbitai-token-sample.csv (CSV, 72KB), prompt-length-sample.txt (TXT, 9KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Simran Kaur <simran@orbitai.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help — session shapes + quantization limits

Simran — thanks for the sample, this is great context. Quick notes and a small ask before we size: 

1) We'll populate our sizer template (attached) but need a handful of telemetry rows to make a reliable occupancy estimate:
   - per-request latency distribution (P50, P90, P99) for both text-gen and chat-session continuation paths
   - per-session average request rate (requests/min) and fraction that are multi-turn (>3 rounds)
   - percent of responses that are streaming vs single-shot

2) Quantization: int8 is broadly safe for the models most teams use; int4 can give meaningful cost wins but we need to know quality sensitivity — do you have a small eval prompt set we can run after quantizing?

3) Can you confirm SLA targets (e.g., 99.5% p99 latency under committed capacity) and any hard outage tolerances?

I'm attaching our "redwood-sizer-template.xlsx" — fill the highlighted sheets and we'll run a quick pass and return a committed-capacity estimate plus split by model SKU and quantization profile.

I'll loop Marissa for cost/rate-card guidance and Karthik for technical constraints (batching, KV cache behavior).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-sizer-template.xlsx (XLSX, 140KB)

From: Simran Kaur <simran@orbitai.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Adam Li <adam@orbitai.ai>, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Sep 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing help — session shapes + quantization limits

Thanks Jonas — uploaded the sizer with the requested rows (sheet "telemetry_sample"). A few clarifications:

- The latency values in telemetry are from our current cloud host (non-optimized). We expect Redwood to be ~20-30% faster once tuned.
- About 18% of sessions are multi-turn >5 rounds; 7% of requests are streaming (partial responses).
- SLA target is 99.9% availability and a goal of p99 < 750ms under committed throughput.

I've cc'd Camila (our account lead) to help schedule a short sizing workshop and share the full telemetry bucket if you need it.

attached: redwood-sizer-template.xlsx (filled), orbitai-token-sample.csv (updated)

— Simran

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 Sep 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quantization & burst-floor recommendation for OrbitAI

Internal note — tagging here for the sizing workshop:

- If OrbitAI's quality eval shows <1% delta on top-1 tokens post-int8, recommend int8 as default for production commit. We can stage int4 on a canary fraction (5-10%) for further cost optimization if latency/throughput targets require it.
- For the 10-min spikes to 1.8k concurrent sessions, we should propose a modest burst pool (20-25% of committed) with autoscale back to committed within 30m. This reduces commit size while preserving SLA during marketing-driven spikes.
- Karthik: can you confirm whether session KV warmup for their multi-turn profile favors keeping a portion of sessions pinned (session-affinity) vs purely pooling? If affinity helps p99, call it out.

I'll draft the cost split (committed vs burst) and include the per-token cost delta for int8 vs int4.

— Marissa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 27 Sep 2028 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quantization & burst-floor recommendation for OrbitAI

Quick technical addendum for the workshop agenda:

- For multi-turn-heavy workloads (18% >5 rounds), KV cache hit-rate matters more than raw batch size. I'd recommend we instrument session KV lifetime and cold-start latency; if their average inter-request gap per session is <60s, affinity + warmed shards provide best p99.
- If they want to push int4, we'll need to reserve a separate canary model variant to compare semantic drift metrics (ROUGE / task-specific metric) against their eval prompts. Int4 is attractive for throughput but increases failure modes for sampling-heavy responses.
- Action: schedule a 60-min sizing workshop with telemetry walkthrough and a live canary plan. I can run the kernel-selection notes during the call.

— Karthik
Senior Inferencing Engineer, Redwood Inference
